content: On April 23rd, a Russian SU-27 fighter aggressively approached a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk, demonstrating its armaments, in an incident that occurred against the backdrop of tensions between the US and Russia over Ukraine.

Prince Charles and Camilla will embark on a 12-day royal tour of Australia and New Zealand, including visits to 12 towns and cities, to celebrate the Prince's 67th birthday and mark his 15th visit to the region, where they will also meet the new Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull.
A 70-something woman attacked in Sneem, County Kerry on September 20th has led to the detention of a suspect found in Killarney and being questioned by police.

Hugh McGoldrick, a former GP whose name has been erased from the medical register due to falsifying drug trial results for sleep disorder patients, has failed to appeal the decision, leading to its enforcement.

A body was found in a wooded area near Dorking, and a 21-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of murder, with additional questioning permitted as the police await the results of a post-mortem examination.

Josh Hanson, a man from north-west London, died after being stabbed in the neck at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, with police urging witnesses from the night to come forward with any information.
Hovertravel is considering adding a cross-Solent ferry service between Sandown and Southsea on selected days in July and August to boost tourism, pending approval and finalization of details.

Police are investigating an attack on a victim in the Heights area at 2:00 AM on Sunday, involving up to eight assailants, and have arrested and subsequently bailed a 30-year-old man while appealing for more information.

As monsoon rains continue to impact millions across India, the death toll from recent floods in Gujarat has risen significantly, affecting over 450,000 people, with some beginning to return to their homes as waters recede.

To celebrate its 25th anniversary, the Premier League's 2017-2018 season kicks off with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on a Friday night at 19:45 BST, while Sky Sports broadcasts 10 such matches under their multi-million-pound deal, reflecting the league's growing popularity and the increasing use of unofficial streams among fans.
Oldham Athletic dismissed Cristian Montano, a 22-year-old player involved in spot-fixing allegations, after a thorough internal investigation, despite his previous contributions to the team.

A 20-year-old man named Rick Edwards has been sentenced to a suspended jail term and supervised probation after admitting to starting a fire at the former Pontins resort in Brixham, which destroyed much of the 42-acre site and increased demolition costs due to extensive damage.

Former Celtic player Wilson, aged 30, returned to Nottingham Forest in 2013 for £2.5m but is currently out of football after being released in May, having played 51 games for the club in his second stint there.
Australia's Chris Faulkner took a remarkable performance by dismissing three Sri Lankan batsmen in quick succession to help his team win by 82 runs and level the five-match series at 1-1.

Sale Sharks' 32-year-old Moldovan international forward Vadim Cobilas is leaving the team to join French Top 14 side Bordeaux, while the club is in talks to retain several key players for next season.

India's dominant start collapsed as they lost their last seven wickets for just 20 runs, allowing Australia to secure a comfortable victory and a 4-0 series win despite a strong performance from Aaron Finch and David Warner.

Safety concerns over potential debris from a large fire that killed at least 58 people in a 24-story building led to the suspension of parts of the London Underground's Hammersmith and City and Circle Lines.
Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old player with a history at both Kilmarnock and Hearts, is set to return to Rugby Park after signing a three-year contract, marking his 150th appearance for the club.

While celebrating Paul Anderson's goal during an Ipswich vs Norwich match, Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling with a celebratory leap, and Anderson offered to pay for the repairs.

Retailers in Wales must now keep cigarettes out of public view unless requested by a customer, with non-compliance punishable by fines and imprisonment, and the move is supported by health officials who believe it will reduce the appeal of smoking.

Wood's Luke Garrard believes that Lucas, who has previously scored three goals in ten appearances for the National League side and made his Bristol Rovers debut in 2014, will provide goal-scoring options and challenge defenses at their current level.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovations including waterproofing, removing and rebuilding the signal box chimney, and nighttime platform canopy work to preserve its historical charm while minimizing disruption.

Lawrence Phillips, a once-promising NFL player turned troubled ex-con, was found dead in his prison cell, leaving behind a legacy marked by both athletic achievement and personal struggles with the law and inner demons.

The Northern Ireland Transport Minister has proposed extending bus lane operating hours for the Belfast Rapid Transit system from 12 hours to 16 hours per day, with plans for two rounds of consultation and potential flexibility in implementation.

Lionel Messi scored his 287th La Liga goal for Barcelona to extend his lead as the competition's all-time top scorer, securing a victory against Atletico despite an early goal from Torres, while Cristiano Ronaldo also scored his club's record 230th league goal for Real Madrid.

Italian authorities have arrested over 70 people, including players, club officials, and potentially a police officer, as part of an investigation into a suspected match-fixing ring involving clubs from lower-tier divisions and allegedly linked to the 'Ndrangheta mafia.

Thousands of hybrid Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings, bred in a kitchen and a laboratory, were released into dykes at Castle Marshes to enhance genetic diversity and improve adaptation to climate change, supported by Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and the BBC Wildlife Fund.

The Partition of India in 1947 led to the creation of two independent countries and resulted in millions of people becoming refugees, as seen through the personal story of one family in a Newsround special on CBBC.

Iva Barr, a long-time marathon runner, completed 14 miles of the London Marathon before finishing the remaining distance by walking, and despite not completing the full route, she cherished the experience and had no regrets.

In China's hottest property markets, couples are resorting to fake divorces to buy more homes, despite efforts by the central bank to control prices, making housing unaffordable for many young workers earning low wages.

A 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder after a landlord, Mr. Jones, died following a stand-off with police at a pub in Holyhead, and officers are seeking witnesses from a bus that passed through the area during the incident.
The article provides information on following the BBC Entertainment news channel on social media and suggests that if you have a story suggestion, you can email them.

In a tragic accident near Carsphairn, a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, 46-year-old Scott Kennedy and 50-year-old Antony Sztuka, with the van driver later dying in hospital, and the road being reopened later that day; investigators are seeking witnesses, particularly those who saw a white flat-bed pickup truck in the area.
Sarah Tait, the Australian rower who won an Olympic silver medal and battled cervical cancer, served as an inspiration to many athletes both during her competitive career and beyond.

In Kabul, two Taliban bombings targeting buses injured multiple individuals and occurred shortly after Afghan President Ashraf Ghani signed an agreement allowing US troops to remain in the country post-2014.
Daimler reported strong overall sales growth despite slowing demand in China, predicting significant full-year sales and maintaining confidence in future growth despite emerging market slowdowns.

A lifeguard intervened to save the 10-year-old son of Crown Prince Frederik from a rip current on the Gold Coast, an incident that drew public attention despite Danish officials downplaying the prince's potential risk.
A fire in Elgin Road, involving an elderly man whose body was found inside, has occurred with no reports of suspicious circumstances as of the initial investigation.

Veterans with complex amputation-related medical issues can now receive specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre in Surrey, enhancing their access to advanced care after being referred from their NHS providers.

Four speed enforcement cameras on a section of the M4 in Port Talbot have caught around 125 speeding drivers per day since going live, marking a decrease from the 700 per day recorded during the trial period, according to the Wales Road Casualty Reduction Partnership GoSafe.

A British teacher in Spain was arrested after police uncovered a large number of sexually explicit images involving minors, including those of students and a specific girl he had a special obsession with, following an Interpol investigation into illegal file sharing.
A sturgeon named Steve, valued at up to £1,000, was found in a puddle near a car wash after escaping from a shopping center during floods, though a larger koi carp named Chadwick remains at large.

Comedian Chris Rock, who has been married to Malaak Compton-Rock for 19 years, has filed for divorce while maintaining a request for privacy as they work through the process with their two daughters, Lola and Zahra.
A collision occurred on the motorway between junctions 13 and 14, causing closures and traffic disruptions, with police requesting witnesses to come forward.

The Vatican has not approved France's nomination of Laurent Stefanini as its new ambassador, potentially due to concerns over his liberal stance on homosexuality, which contrasts with the traditional conservative position of the Catholic Church.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day fall since April 2014, closing down 2.4%, despite a significant rise in Kraft Foods' share price following its merger agreement with Heinz, while other sectors like semiconductors and biotech saw sharp declines.

Czech player Martina Vondrousova defeated Estonia's Anett Kontaveit to advance in the tournament, bringing her ranking close to the top 100, while Croatia's Borna Coric won his first ATP title by overcoming a significant deficit against Philipp Kohlschreiber in the final.

Stoke City have signed Cameroon striker Eric Choupo-Moting, a player they had attempted to sign four years earlier, as their fourth summer transfer following the arrivals of Darren Fletcher, Kurt Zouma, and Josh Tymon.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy who died at a Maine private nursing home in September of last year was posthumously treated as a murder victim after the police began questioning a suspect following the results of an autopsy in April.

Heavy rains and flooding in Chennai, India, and neighboring Sri Lanka have forced evacuations, closed institutions, and prompted the government to allocate significant relief funds as rescue operations continue.

The driver of a McGill's 904 bus kept all passengers safe when the vehicle caught fire outside Largs, ensuring they evacuated quickly while the bus burned and popped and banged, with no injuries reported.

Notts' Jake Ball, after impressively taking six wickets in each of the team's first two games and leading the bowling in the County Championship, is now expected to spearhead the new ball attack alongside Stuart Broad.

An estimated 120 "Jersey Pals" perished in the Battle of the Somme, and their sacrifice is commemorated by a memorial stone made from Jersey granite, unveiled in France, with a portion of it planned to be returned to Jersey for inclusion in a monument in Royal Square.

Actor John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and is currently filming Episode VIII, returned to his former theater company, Theatre Peckham, to mentor young actors and inspire the next generation, even doing a Chewbacca impression for Newsround.

English golfer Luke Donald leads the European Tour event after a strong round, with multiple players close behind including 21-year-old Mark Fitzpatrick and former world number ones Lee Westwood and Luke Donald himself.

Middlesex gained a strong foothold in the match with a 279-run partnership between Voges and Malan, leaving them well-placed for their first County Championship win of the season despite early setbacks for the opening batsmen.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy remains critically injured after a tragic incident on Penilee Road, leading to the identification of a 54-year-old man by police who is now in the Dumfries and Galloway area.

The childhood home of a Beatle, located on Newcastle Road in Wavertree and known to be just a few streets away from Penny Lane, was sold at auction through a bidding war, with an anonymous phone bidder purchasing it for an undisclosed amount within a guide price range of £150,000 to £250,000.

Aaron Joseph, who denies owning the dog that attacked David Ellam, leading to his death, appeared at Leeds Crown Court where he also admitted possession of cannabis, with a trial set for February 5th.
Thomas Bebbington, a 22-year-old from Shrewsbury, was last seen entering a river near Dana Steps and his body was found by a member of the public about 10 miles away from Shrewsbury on private land.

Five-week-old otters, despite needing frequent feeding, are developing well and are expected to eventually move to a larger outdoor enclosure with a pool where they will be fed live food in the coming months.

A 33-year-old woman named Joanne Thompson, who is a mother of four, was discovered at her home in Newtownards by a relative on Wednesday, and police are seeking witnesses to events surrounding a nearby bonfire and potential disturbances near her residence.
This spring, an unprecedented 2,270 black-tailed godwits, nearly doubling the previous record, stopped off on the Scottish island of Tiree to refuel during their migration to Iceland.

Rangers' long-serving coach Steve Durrant, who has been associated with the club for over a decade in various capacities, is being let go by new manager Mark Warburton, who aims to change the coaching staff.
An albino deer, a rare occurrence estimated to happen once every 100,000 births, has drawn much attention from visitors.

Asad Khan, a student from Bradford who died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School, was reportedly bullied and expressed feeling unsafe and that life was hard before his death, leading to an ongoing inquest where the alleged bully may be called to testify.

A unique, historically significant 1654 coronation painting, believed to have been in Rokeby Park since at least 1880, remains a mystery regarding its origin and creator despite recent restoration and expert examination.
Macclesfield Town defeated Wrexham 3-0, lifting them to seventh place in the table and leaving Wrexham in 15th.

Total has become the headline sponsor of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) for an undisclosed amount, taking over from Orange and committing to support the development and growth of African football through their partnership.

Former Porto boss Luis Enrique has named a new Spain national team squad featuring experienced players like David de Gea, Diego Costa, and Andrés Iniesta, ahead of upcoming friendly matches against Belgium and Liechtenstein.

A large, deliberate wildfire has broken out in an area spanning five kilometers, involving multiple fire crews from both British and Irish services, and has been linked to other recent wildfires in the region.

After suffering from cramp and losing favor with England, 31-year-old bowler Rankin is returning to play for Ireland in time for the World Twenty20, hoping to contribute to their potential bid for Test status.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, established by the Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership and the Patient Client Council, seeks to improve treatment and care for those with rare diseases and provide a unified voice for affected families.

Gloucester Cathedral is expanding its choir to include girls for the first time, aiming to discover talented young singers from diverse backgrounds and provide them with opportunities to sing in the cathedral's services.

Chelsea's 29-year-old winger Pedro was hospitalized after suffering from an unspecified injury during a 3-0 win in Beijing but has since returned to London wearing a protective mask, while the rest of the team continues their tour with matches against Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.
Nottinghamshire has appointed James Taylor and Paul Sales to work with the batsmen, leveraging their extensive cricket experience to provide valuable guidance and improve the team's performance.

A man has been charged with multiple offenses, including criminal damage and assault on police, after an incident witnessed by prescription pick-up attendees, including children, on Whiterock Road in Belfast on Friday afternoon.

A yacht's engine failure near Muck Island prompted a successful rescue operation by the Larne RNLI, involving both inshore and all-weather lifeboats, which towed the vessel to safety at Carrick Marina.

The article describes a closely contested football match between Ipswich and MK Dons, ending with Ipswich winning 3-2, despite both managers expressing dissatisfaction with their team's performance and the season overall.

A motorcyclist was injured when a bridge collapsed onto the M25 motorway, prompting charges against the bridge owner including dangerous driving and criminal damage, with the road remaining closed for several days for clearance and removal of debris.
Several Germans organized a flash mob in Platja d'Aro, Spain, pretending to chase celebrities with selfie sticks, causing a panic and stampede among holidaymakers, resulting in injuries and arrests.

Two adults, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze McGregor, appeared in court charged with the murder of two-and-a-half-year-old Jeremiah Regis, who was found with over 100 injuries and died from blunt force trauma.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, fueled by high winds, forced evacuations and required significant firefighting resources, with multiple injuries reported and efforts expected to continue through the night.
The British Speedway Promoters' Association and Leicester Speedway have reached an agreement and signed a 15-year lease for the team's venue, marking a potential new chapter for the club.
Charles Gordon, 51, appeared in court charged with the murder of Elizabeth Bowe, 50, and his police response is now under investigation by the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner.

Jim O'Brien, a 29-year-old midfielder with experience from Celtic and Motherwell, has signed a two-year contract with Ross County after a successful loan spell last season, bringing valuable experience to the team.

Northamptonshire restricted Durham to a low score of 59-3 in the first innings, capitalizing on Durham's struggling batting lineup, while Northants themselves narrowly avoided further losses in their reply before bad light ended play early.
New Zealand golfer Lydia Ko is one shot behind the joint leaders after two rounds of the LPGA Championship, with only five players under par at the halfway stage.

Scottish footballer Alan Watson has accepted a role as assistant coach to Scotland's national team, working alongside manager Gordon Strachan and assistant Mark McGhee, with Watson bringing his extensive experience from previous roles to support the team's World Cup qualification efforts.

The Belfast Giants secured a dominant victory over Braehead Clan with four second-period goals, leaving the Devils in a challenging position as they prepare for back-to-back games against Manchester Storm and Coventry Blaze.

Defending champion Jordan Spieth suffered a shocking collapse at the Masters, dropping a quadruple-bogey on the 12th hole after leading by five shots, allowing Danny Willett to become the first Englishman to win the tournament since 1996.

The BBC invites submissions of recent photographs through various platforms, offering to publish them under certain terms while acknowledging contributors' copyright and reserving the right to edit content and reject submissions.

The prosecution argues that an optometrist failed to detect signs of Vinnie Barker's fatal brain condition during a routine eye test, alleging her misconduct amounted to criminal gross negligence manslaughter.

Food price inflation in China rose to 4.9% in June from 3.2% in May, partly due to increasing pork prices, though still below the government's target, potentially limiting interest rate cuts despite missing some analysts' expectations.
Senegal striker Cisse and others paid tribute to the late Cheick Tiote at a memorial service, with Cisse describing Tiote as a brother and sharing his memories of their time together at Newcastle.

In stage five of the cycling race, Slovakian rider Michael Sagan won the stage and moved up to second overall, with Colombian Nairo Quintana maintaining the lead, followed by Thibaut Pinot in second place.
Cuadrilla's fracking project at Preston New Road in Lancashire, despite a pending legal challenge, has moved forward with plans to invest in the local economy, while opponents remain skeptical.

Three teenage boys from north-west London, who were suspected of planning to travel to Syria, were arrested upon returning to the UK after being stopped by Turkish officials, and were later released without charge, in contrast to three London schoolgirls who had previously traveled to Istanbul with similar intentions.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital highlighted what he perceived as excessive spending on a blackout blind, which was later bought for a fraction of the original quoted price, sparking debate about healthcare funding and expenditure.
Swansea City's youth team achieved a cup final victory and secured 31 wins across all competitions in the 2016-17 season, a stark contrast to the senior team's narrow escape from relegation.

Following severe storms in December 2013 that damaged the dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system to reduce the risk of future flooding, as discussions with Natural Resources Wales indicate the need for additional defenses due to the narrowness of the existing dunes.

South Shields, an eighth-tier football team captained by Julio Arca, will host an FA Cup match against Bridlington Town on August 19th, with commentary from Match of the Day’s Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, and the game available to stream live across various BBC platforms.
Police are investigating a potential targeted attack on two men in Edinburgh, with one suffering serious facial injuries, as they seek witnesses and information about suspicious activity in the area.

Pamela McLaggan pleaded guilty to manslaughter upon being found guilty of killing Jonathan Baines, known as "Willy," whose body was discovered on August 1st in Gainsborough after he had been out at races and in pubs.
A 15-year-old boy was assaulted by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries and having his mobile phone stolen after being punched and stamped on while on a train.

A Dewsbury teenager was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April and bailed, while two other 17-year-olds from the same area who disappeared in March are suspected of joining ISIS, linking the cases to ongoing counter-terrorism investigations.

The Belfast Giants have selected a largely returning squad featuring key players like Jonathan Boxill, Craig Peacock, Colin Shields, and Stephen Murphy for upcoming matches against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia, with the winners progressing to final qualifying for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang, Korea.

Matthew Perry may not appear in the upcoming Friends tribute special, while his former co-stars are set to participate in the show honoring the late James Burrows, and Perry is starring in a new play called "The End of Longing" that will run in London's West End.

Veteran midfielder Jones, who played a key role in Burnley's Championship-winning season and started their Premier League opener, has a diverse career spanning multiple clubs including Manchester United, having joined Burnley in 2013 after Wigan.

Joe Acquaro, a well-known lawyer and cafe owner in Melbourne's Italian community, was shot dead, with investigators suggesting possible involvement from underworld bosses, despite a previous gangland feud having ended over a decade ago.

The Air France 777-200, carrying 294 passengers from Paris to Vancouver, was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight burning smell was detected on board, landing normally and prompting the airline to arrange for the passengers to be transferred to another aircraft to continue their journey.

A severe weather warning has been issued for Wales as remnants of Hurricane Gonzalo bring strong winds and heavy rain, with gusts exceeding 55mph expected inland and up to 70mph in coastal areas, potentially disrupting travel and causing travel disruptions.

The article describes a visit to a children's hospital in Sheffield to explore concerns about overcrowding and its impact on patient care, including interviews with a doctor and children who recently needed medical treatment.

Kenneth David Dickie, 64, was found with a serious head injury at Rockley Park in Poole and died at Southampton General Hospital, while a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman have been charged or bailed in connection with the incident.

Cardiff City have retained forward Macheda until the end of the season while signing David Vaughan to a one-year contract, though their pursuit of Andre Moritz was unsuccessful due to contract issues.
Christopher Huxtable's body was found after the building collapse, providing closure to his family while highlighting the ongoing uncertainty for the families of the two remaining missing men.
Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of securing a win against QPR to close the gap on competing teams, while noting key player absences and uncertainties for both teams.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano described his experience walking in space as absolutely fantastic and exciting after participating in two spacewalks, orbiting Earth 2,656 times, and traveling over 110 million kilometers during his 2013 mission to the International Space Station.

England Knights player Joe Arundel, who made his debut at 16 and played 44 games for Hull Kingston Rovers (referred to as Tigers), is excited but nervous about joining Hull FC, where he will be expected to contribute to building a long-term winning culture.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of RBS, is working to update approximately 600,000 delayed payments for affected customers by Saturday, following an IT issue that also impacted RBS and NatWest customers in 2012.
Tanzania defeated Kenya 2-1 in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, while Ethiopia secured third place with a 4-1 win over Uganda.
McDonald's in Japan is rationing French fries due to a potato supply shortage caused by industrial action in the US, with additional potato imports expected to arrive by January.

The Classic race purse is increased to £1.625 million with the addition of top contenders Permian and Khalidi, while trainer John Jenkins defends running a 1,000-1 outsider, Diore Lia, for charity despite her limited racing record.

Atletico Madrid star Antoine Griezmann, who leads La Liga in goals for his team and is set to miss a match against Real Madrid and France's friendly due to a foot injury, will begin treatment on Monday.
Veteran Australian prop Willie Mason, known for his aggression and physical play, joins the Huddersfield Giants' Super League side, aiming to bolster the team's group quality after recent losses.

A survey by The Marine Conservation Society found an 11% increase in dog feces on UK beaches, with a 71% rise in Scotland specifically, but noted that pet owners are improving by using plastic bags, though they should now aim to dispose of these properly in designated bins rather than leaving them on the beach.

The Supreme Court has ruled that introducing fees for employment tribunal cases was unlawful and unconstitutional, due to their indirect discrimination against women and overall impact on access to justice.
Wycombe Wanderers secured a victory against Dagenham & Redbridge despite being a man down, moving up to sixth place while Dagenham remains in the relegation zone.

Bee-eaters, a species native to southern Europe, have successfully bred at a quarry in southern England for the second consecutive summer, with all chicks having hatched and expected to fledge in the next few weeks.
A kayaker capsized in the River Wey near Guildford, and despite a rescue attempt by a witnessing boy, divers are searching the waters as a flood warning is in place due to recent storms.
A stone thrown by an elephant at Rabat Zoo hit a girl who later died in the hospital, though the zoo maintained that the incident was rare and unpredictable despite meeting international standards.

Labour MP Sarah Glass has been appointed to the shadow cabinet despite growing calls for a leadership election, following the resignation of her predecessor Angela Powell who lost confidence in party leader Jeremy Corbyn.
With six teams vying for the Premier League title, Chelsea manager Conte emphasizes the importance of maintaining focus and avoiding mistakes as they face a challenging match against Burnley.

A dispersal order has been implemented in Llangefni to address anti-social behavior and protect residents from groups of young adults causing disturbances and damage, with powers to remove troublemakers and ban them from the area.

De Roon, a 26-year-old Dutch international who scored five goals in 36 games for Middlesbrough last season, has departed the club after an initial £8.8 million transfer to Teesside in June 2016, with Middlesbrough's manager expressing interest in signing Chelsea's Lewis Baker as a potential replacement.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, a children's humor book award launched in 2008 by Michael Rosen, will be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations, with plans to strengthen its impact and ensure a robust future.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr., a white supremacist who admitted to killing two people and wounding others at Jewish sites in Kansas, was sentenced to death and executed by lethal injection after declaring his belief that Jews had too much power and expressing no remorse.

The city council plans to launch a larger self-service bike scheme in April 2017, featuring 500 bikes accessible from various locations including district centers and universities, modeled after successful programs like London's "Boris bikes."

Senegal international Diaf Sakho, who recently returned to light training after back surgery and missing most of the season, is expected to start a personalized pre-season training regimen before being considered for Premier League selection.

The Northern Ireland residential property market saw an annual price increase of 5.4% in the third quarter of 2016, with the largest rises observed in Antrim and Newtownabbey and the smallest in Ards and North Down, while the average price stood at just over £124,000.
A recent delivery of a wind turbine part in Dumfries and Galloway ended in a ditch, contrasting with a successful bridge crossing earlier in the year.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is consulting the public on potential downgrades to hospital services due to staffing shortages, despite a legal challenge that temporarily blocked plans to reduce maternity care at one hospital, with residents expressing concerns about increased travel for care.
Mignon du Preez scored a second ODI century to help South Africa post a commanding 272-6 against Ireland, who managed only 204 all out.

Three-time Commonwealth Games silver medalist Peake aims to break her Welsh high jump record and secure a place on the British team for the Rio Olympics by achieving a personal best of at least 4.50 meters this weekend.
A large fire at a building site in Bloomery Circle, Llanwern, believed to have been deliberately set and fueled by scrapped railway sleepers, burned for over 10 hours before being extinguished.

A concert and charity event were held in Edinburgh to commemorate the victims of the Nepal earthquake and raise funds for relief efforts, featuring the traditional Singing Bowl Concert at St Giles' Cathedral.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's head coach, has been banned from the technical area for the second leg of their Europa League qualifying match against Brondby due to his involvement in an incident where he remonstrated with officials during the first leg.

A fire broke out in the deep-sea Boulby mine, resulting in seven workers being hospitalized, 11 others being temporarily unaccounted for, and the Health and Safety Executive serving an improvement notice to the company, which must comply by June 27th.

A British man and a French tourist were caught posing naked at Machu Picchu, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Peru, and questioned by police for offenses against morality, with no arrests or charges made so far.

Croatia international and Barcelona player Ivan Rakitic, who scored 23 goals in 145 appearances for Barcelona, is set to leave the club with a buyout clause of £109 million after making a significant contribution, including in Barcelona's Champions League comeback victory.

A couple from Halstead suffered severe injuries in a robbery attempt where their family members were threatened; police are using a detailed description and a computer-generated image to assist in identifying one of the suspects involved in the crime.

The Wickerman Festival, set to take place at East Kirkcarswell Farm in July, features Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner and includes a diverse lineup of artists such as Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling.

Foden expresses optimism about contributing to the upcoming England squad alongside his fellow Saints teammates, while also acknowledging the potential for further improvement that could benefit both his personal performance and English rugby as a whole.
A motorcyclist died after colliding with a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, while two children in the car were injured, with one remaining in critical condition.

Pfizer has acquired California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose eczema treatment crisaborole could reach $2 billion in annual sales if approved, in what Pfizer sees as an opportunity to address a significant unmet medical need for millions of patients.

Police responded to a volatile street situation in Dagenham, recovering multiple weapons and arresting two boys, while reporting no injuries, with officers emphasizing the potential lifesaving impact of their intervention.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault following a report of an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens in Cardiff early Thursday morning.

John Lamont's resignation from the Scottish Parliament seat leads to a concurrent local council, Scottish Parliament, and Westminster by-election within five weeks, with the Conservative party aiming to unseat the SNP's Calum Kerr.

Canada has lifted its ban on importing beef from the EU, including significant producers like France and Germany, as a welcome move for EU farmers facing financial difficulties due to export declines and a recent €500 million aid package.

European finance ministers have endorsed plans to create a unified EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions and impose sanctions, aiming to address tax avoidance practices revealed by the Panama Papers leak.

Archaeological excavations during the construction of the West Link in Inverness have uncovered pottery fragments, kilns, and Bronze Age burnt mounds, indicating ancient grain-drying practices and possible sauna or hot stone bathing traditions.

Main scored the only goal of the match in the 60th minute after latching onto a pass from Jonathan Forte, securing a win for Oldham against Southend and keeping both teams' positions in League One relatively stable.
The Irish actor Liam Lally, known for his roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and The Secret of Kells, passed away peacefully after a short illness, leaving behind his wife and children.

Derby City Council has decided to keep Moorways Pool open for a year after local campaigners gathered over 4,000 signatures to protest against its closure, despite the council's efforts to find savings elsewhere to meet its financial targets.

UN officials express concern over the detention of children from areas previously controlled by Boko Haram in Nigerian military barracks, highlighting the lack of proper legal process for such detentions.
Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing Motherwell's experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis as cover for the injured Neil Alexander ahead of the Edinburgh derby against Hibernian.

Chelsey Lee, a 26-year-old basketball player who won rookie of the year but was found to have falsified her and her father's birth certificates to appear as having a South Korean grandmother, faces lifetime suspension from the league, along with potential legal action and changes to the league's rules regarding international players.

A new app released by Ofcom alongside its 2015 Connected Nations report highlights that while significant progress has been made in UK home wi-fi speeds and super-fast broadband availability, many homes still experience slower speeds due to interference and lack of infrastructure, particularly in rural areas and among small businesses.

Ibrahimovic, despite his team's underperformance, expressed that pressure from fans and the media motivates him to perform, aiming for individual success while also hoping his team improves its standing.
